statement: A top-3 compute jurisdiction has licensing or pre-approval of frontier training above a compute threshold in force (official gazette; by 2028-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not met at end-2024. Bloc A had only reporting (not approval) duties: an executive-order survey (Jan 2024) and a proposed quarterly reporting rule for training runs >1e26 operations (Sept 2024, not final). The most ambitious sub-national bill (frontier-model safety duties plus a new oversight board) was vetoed in Sept. Bloc B's 2023 interim measures require filing before public-facing generative services launch, but expressly exclude R&D not offered to the public, so they do not license training. A large economic bloc's AI act (in force Aug 2024) presumes systemic risk at a compute threshold and requires notification, not pre-approval.

items.summary: Bloc A's commerce department proposed a rule requiring quarterly notification of planned or ongoing training runs above 1e26 operations and of large computing clusters. Reporting only, no approval; proposed, not in force in 2024. It also confirms a mandatory survey of frontier developers was issued on 2024-01-26.
items.detail: Bloc A BIS, 'Establishment of Reporting Requirements for the Development of Advanced AI Models and Computing Clusters', proposed rule, 89 FR 73612 (FR Doc. 2024-20529), comments closed 2024-10-11; implements EO 14110 s.4.2.

items.summary: The governor of the sub-national jurisdiction home to most leading AI firms vetoed a bill that would have imposed safety duties on developers of large (compute/cost-thresholded) models and created a state board to oversee them, arguing compute thresholds give 'a false sense of security'.
items.detail: California Governor Newsom, SB 1047 veto message, 2024-09-29.

items.summary: Bloc B's interim generative-AI measures (in force since 2023-08-15, operative through 2024) regulate generative services offered to the public, with pre-launch filing; Article 2 excludes organisations that research or develop the technology without offering it to the public. Service filing, not licensing of training.
items.detail: CAC et al., 生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法 (Order No. 15), published 2023-07-13, effective 2023-08-15. Article 2 scope exclusion verified this run. CAC's 2024 filing tally (302 services) was published 2025-01-08, after the phase end, so not used.

items.summary: A large economic bloc (not clearly a top-3 compute jurisdiction) published its AI act; general-purpose models above a training-compute threshold are presumed to carry systemic risk and must be notified and evaluated, but training does not need pre-approval. GPAI obligations apply from Aug 2025.
items.detail: Regulation (Bloc C) 2024/1689 (AI Act), OJ L 2024-07-12, in force 2024-08-01; Art. 51-52 (10^25 FLOP presumption, notification). Page verified this run; threshold article not in the extracted excerpt.
